name: Triage n8n workflow failures with Bright Data and GPT-5.6 to tell an outage from your own bug

parameters.content:
## When a workflow breaks, find out whose fault it is first

Half of all workflow failures are the vendor, not you - and you cannot tell from the error message. This runs the moment any of your workflows fails and answers the only question that matters at 3am: **do I need to fix something, or do I need to wait?**

### How it works

n8n hands this workflow the failure. It reads the real payload - the failing node, the HTTP code and the exact URL that was called - and classifies it.

If an external service was involved, **Bright Data fetches that same URL from a clean external IP**. That is the part your own server cannot do for you: if the site answers fine from outside but not from your n8n, that is a network or credential problem, not an outage. It also reads the vendor's own Statuspage for a declared incident.

GPT-5.6 turns all of it into two sentences, and a Switch sends the verdict to the right place: a vendor outage goes to the incident channel, your own bug goes to the dev channel, a rate limit goes to ops. A Code node failure never triggers any of the lookups - no external call means nobody to blame.

### Setup

1. Import this, add a Bright Data Header Auth credential, an OpenAI credential and a Slack credential.

2. **Activate this workflow.** An inactive error workflow is silently skipped.

3. On each workflow you want covered: Settings → Error Workflow → pick this one.

4. In **Settings** here, set the three Slack channels and list your own domains.

## 1. Another workflow just failed
No schedule and no webhook. n8n runs this one when something else breaks, and hands it the failed execution.

## 2. What actually broke
The failing node, the HTTP code and the exact URL that was called. A Code node failure carries none of those, which is how it is recognised.

## 3. Ask the internet, not your own server
Bright Data fetches the same URL from a clean external IP. If it answers there but not for you, the service is fine and something on your side is not.

## 4. What the vendor admits
Statuspage answers /api/v2/summary.json the same way everywhere. A declared incident settles the argument before anyone opens the code.

## 5. One verdict, from whatever evidence exists
Both paths meet here. The verdict is built from named findings, and it never upgrades a guess into a fact.

## 6. Two sentences for whoever was paged
What broke and what to do right now. The model is told to stay inside the evidence and never invent a cause.

## 7. Three answers, three places
An outage belongs in the incident channel, your own bug in the dev channel, a rate limit in ops. They need different people and different urgency.

## An inactive error workflow never runs

This is the one that costs an afternoon. Save this workflow, select it as the Error Workflow on another workflow, break that workflow deliberately - and nothing happens. No error, no retry, nothing in the UI.

The n8n log says it plainly: `Calling Error Workflow ... is not active and cannot be executed`. An Error Trigger workflow has no schedule and no webhook, so activating it feels wrong, but it is required. Toggle **Active** on.

Verified live on 2026-08-24: identical failure, inactive handler, zero executions; activated, the very next failure came straight through.
